# The Box

> The Box is a sovereign, self-hosting personal-server platform. One generic OS
> image installs any machine; identity arrives at first boot. Every change is an
> atomic, reversible Nix generation. A running Box exposes a dashboard, a JSON
> API, and an MCP server, so an agent can provision and manage it end to end.

This file is written for AI agents. If you are an agent asked to "set up The Box"
on a machine, everything you need is here. Complete machine reference (orders
schema + every MCP tool): https://thebox.build/llms-full.txt

## Provision a spare machine into a Box

Requirements: SSH access to the target (as root, or a sudo user), plus `ssh` and
`curl` locally. The takeover **wipes the target disk**, so only run it on a machine
you intend to convert.

If `boxd` is installed locally, one command runs the whole flow and prints
`{address, token, mcp_url, dashboard}`, then skip to "Manage a Box":

    boxd provision root@TARGET_IP --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --json

Without `boxd`, the identical flow with shell tools:

1. Invent a one-time pairing code and build the orders. `erase_disk:true` is
   required consent; `enrollment_code_hash` is the SHA-256 of the code (keep the
   plaintext, which you redeem in step 4):

       CODE=$(head -c5 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')   # keep this
       HASH=$(printf %s "$CODE" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
       KEY=$(cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub)
       cat > box-install.json <<JSON
       { "erase_disk": true, "hostname": "auto",
         "ssh_authorized_keys": ["$KEY"],
         "enrollment_code_hash": "$HASH" }
       JSON

2. Ship the orders and run the takeover installer over SSH. It kexecs into the
   installer, so the SSH connection drops mid-command. That is expected.
   Connecting as root (shown here); as a sudo user, use `sudo BOX_ORDERS_B64=$B64 sh`:

       B64=$(base64 -w0 box-install.json)
       ssh root@TARGET_IP "curl -fsSL https://thebox.build/install.sh | BOX_ORDERS_B64=$B64 sh"

3. Wait for the Box to come up on management port 2693 (health is public):

       until curl -fsS http://TARGET_IP:2693/api/v1/health >/dev/null; do sleep 5; done

4. Redeem your code for a session token:

       TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -X POST http://TARGET_IP:2693/pair/redeem \
         -H 'accept: application/json' --data-urlencode "code=$CODE" | jq -r .token)

## Bare metal: a machine with no OS

A blank machine has no SSH to hit. A human flashes/netboots the installer once
(https://thebox.build/docs/install.html#bare-metal); from there it's agent-drivable
on the LAN. While it sits in setup it **beacons over mDNS** as an unclaimed Box
installer, and its setup API is PIN-gated (the PIN is shown on the machine's screen,
or set in the Configurator, and you supply it out of band).

1. Discover it (its address comes straight from the browse record):

       avahi-browse -rpt _thebox-setup._tcp | grep '^=' | grep IPv4

2. Confirm what you found (no PIN needed):

       curl -fsS http://IP:2693/api/hello        # {"thebox":"installer","state":"unclaimed","pin_required":true}

3. Build orders as above (§ code/HASH/KEY), then push them with a layout and the
   setup PIN. This commits and starts the install:

       curl -fsS -X POST http://IP:2693/api/commit -H "x-setup-pin: $PIN" \
         -H 'content-type: application/json' \
         -d "{\"layout\":\"single\",\"base\":$(cat box-install.json)}"

Then wait for the Box to come up (step 3–4 of "Provision") and redeem your code
for a session token. Layouts: single | mirror | pool.

## Manage a Box: configure, deploy, maintain

Every Box runs an MCP server (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP) at http://BOX:2693/mcp.
Authenticate with the session token as a Bearer header: `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`.
This is the same declarative surface the dashboard and CLI use.

List the tools:

    curl -fsS -X POST http://BOX:2693/mcp \
      -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'

Deploy a static site (activates atomically as a new generation; rollback-safe):

    curl -fsS -X POST http://BOX:2693/mcp -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{
           "name":"deploy_static_site",
           "arguments":{"name":"welcome","index_html":"<h1>hi</h1>"}}}'

Publish a project you just built — send the BUILT output, not the source tree.
Text files are plain strings; binaries are {"base64":"..."}:

    curl -fsS -X POST http://BOX:2693/mcp -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{
           "name":"upload_files",
           "arguments":{"name":"portfolio","files":{
             "index.html":"<h1>hi</h1>",
             "assets/app.js":"console.log(1)"}}}}'

When something is wrong, read the logs rather than guessing:

    …"name":"service_logs","arguments":{"name":"portfolio","lines":50}

Tools: get_status, list_services, list_templates, deploy, deploy_static_site,
upload_files, service_logs, delete_service, list_generations, list_history,
channel_status, channel_check, rollback, backup_status, backup_snapshots,
backup_now, backup_restore.
Full argument schemas + examples: https://thebox.build/llms-full.txt

## Notes

- The Box trusts YOU, not other machines. The session token is a revocable
  operator device. It appears under Devices and can be revoked anytime. Give
  each agent its own SSH key and its own token.
- No account, no phone-home. Keys, codes, and the backup key are generated on the
  Box or by you and never leave it.
- Deploys and platform updates are atomic generations; a bad change is one
  `rollback` away, and a failed update rolls itself back.
- A service that needs the system to run it (a container, an app) reports
  `state` and a `note` saying so until the Box has applied it. Believe the
  state, not the fact that the call succeeded, and read `url` for where it is
  actually served — it is not `/sites/<name>/` for anything but a static site.
- To reach a service from the internet, give it a `domain`, set `public`, and
  point a tunnel at the Box's port 80.
- Bare metal with a blank disk has no SSH to hit. See "Bare metal" below.
